payload.rationale: The brief sets a dreaming-stage reader and names the free magazine as the primary CTA, matching the services.md early-stage rule. It sits mid-article once the history and the 'how many' decision are done, so the invitation follows useful content rather than interrupting it. The Advisor is the in-context secondary after the destination section, where asking friends to travel makes planning abroad a live question; the panel's sceptic found the old line too emotional, so it now reads plainly. All Advisor copy stays within brand-facts.md: single point of contact, works in the couple's time zone, quotes in AUD, fee agreed in writing before any work begins, inclusions confirmed in writing. Nothing implies legal, church or paperwork help, and nothing says the Advisor is present on the day or arranges attendants' travel (deferred per the panel). Weighted enquiry likelihood is 2.0, expected for an informational tradition post, so no further asks are added. The panel's uhnw reader found 'free' mass-market but the panel kept it; the closing magazine sentence keeps 'free' to match the primary. Ideal magnet not on the site: a printable 'asking your bridesmaids to travel' conversation checklist (timing, who covers what, time off, insurance and passport checks) (suggestion only, not placed).
